okr.objective: Corra is an Irish heroine or goddess defeated by St. Patrick.

text: Corra appears in Irish legend as a heroine or a goddess. St. Patrick subdued her while she flew overhead. He cast his silver bell and dragged her down onto Croagh Patrick, the peak that now carries his name. She then sank in Lough Corra, a lake lying at the mountain's foot. A different account holds that Patrick hunted her across the whole island until at last she perished in Lough Derg. That water also sheltered the serpent Caoranach, whose name links to hers. This could explain the claim that Patrick drove Ireland's snakes away, though reptiles never dwelt there (see Serpent). Some read Corra as a Mother Goddess, a figure whose authority collapsed when patriarchal Christianity advanced.
